item.title: Euronews: 14 people missing after Russian drone strike on Kyiv region
item.description: Timur Tkachenko, the head of the Kyiv Regional Military Administration, said the body of one person had been recovered from the rubble and that three people had been injured.

item.title: Euronews: Latest news bulletin | November 22nd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 22nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Euronews: Mongolia faces snap presidential vote as outgoing leader calls for constitutional reform
item.description: Mongolia is preparing for its first early presidential election after President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa resigned amid corruption allegations, having called for constitutional reform before leaving office.

item.title: Euronews: Ukraine: Up to seven feared trapped beneath rubble near Kyiv after Russian attack
item.description: A Russian strike partially destroyed an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, on Sunday. Nine people, including a child, were evacuated as rescuers searched the rubble for up to seven others feared trapped.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Brussels, Charleroi airports to cancel most flights Monday amid Belgian strike
item.description: Air traffic controllers will join a nationwide protest against government spending cuts, prompting anger from airport operators over the last-minute disruption.

item.title: Euronews: Euronews' Attila Kert picked to lead Hungary's public broadcaster
item.description: Euronews Hungary head Attila Kert has been picked to run Hungary's public broadcaster, which faces an overhaul after years of bias criticism under Viktor Orbán. He pledges to restore credibility, launch streaming and probe Russian influence.

item.title: Euronews: Japan: Mascot mania takes over Saitama with 200 colourful characters
item.description: More than 200 colourful mascots gathered in Saitama, Japan, delighting tens of thousands of fans with dancing, parades and photo opportunities. Among the stars was Kumamon, the country's famous black bear mascot.

item.title: Euronews: Tracking site says Iranian tanker reportedly sailing through Strait of Hormuz does not exist
item.description: The US military said Saturday marked 130 consecutive days of its naval blockade against Iran, which it says is preventing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting "billions of dollars in crude oil."

item.title: POLITICO Europe: 14 missing after Russian strike as Zelenskyy presses US over Patriot missiles
item.description: Following the attack near Kyiv, Ukraine's president issued a plea to Washington to authorize air defense missiles financed by allies.

item.title: Euronews: Portugal: Workers brave downpours to demand a more affordable life
item.description: Thousands of people marched through Lisbon, Portugal, on Saturday 21 November 2026, braving heavy rain to demand higher wages, better pensions and measures to tackle the rising cost of living. The demonstration came just days before Portugal's parliamentary budget vote.

item.title: Euronews: Reported FBI hack 'not good' but could have benefits, Trump says
item.description: The reported breach comes amid a wave of tech outages in the US, which have impacted travel, communications and banking, as well as an internal system used by the National Security Agency.

item.title: Euronews: Hot freezers, lost GPS and fake bombs: Europe's month of cyberattacks
item.description: Only three of the incidents tallied by Europe's main tech industry group have been linked to a culprit, and that ambiguity may be the attackers' strongest weapon.

item.title: Euronews: New COP31 draft deal tabled as countries scramble to salvage climate talks
item.description: The latest draft again failed to mention fossil fuels, which have become a flashpoint at the talks.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Europeans dare to believe Trump could deliver security for Ukraine
item.description: After months of anxiety, some of Kyiv's allies now think the U.S will help deliver an acceptable peace.

item.title: Euronews: Gadi Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud party for 'marathon' coalition talks
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot has until early December to form a new government after both his and Netanyahu's blocs fell short of a majority in Israel's October legislative elections.

item.title: Euronews: Madeira's ocean survey finds evidence protection works – and some worrying signs
item.description: A survey by more than 200 specialists found that Madeira's marine reserves are working – but some species are still in peril.

item.title: Euronews: Is Europe ready to judge workers by skills, not just diplomas? Who leads skills-first hiring?
item.description: Employers across Europe increasingly value skills while formal qualifications are still significant. Euronews Business takes a close look at which countries are most ready for a skills-first approach with experts explaining the gaps.

item.title: Euronews: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave UK’ in protest over asylum seeker plans
item.description: Residents of Barnham back symbolic independence vote after government proposes accommodating around 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former RAF base.

item.title: Euronews: A five-star stay in Qatar: Luxury hotels and resorts to book
item.description: From beachfront resorts to skyscraper hotels overlooking the Arabian Gulf, Qatar is home to a growing portfolio of luxury properties.

item.title: Euronews: Ukraine: Dashcam captures massive explosion on Lviv street
item.description: A dashcam captured the moment a Russian projectile struck a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, forcing the driver to reverse. The attack killed two people and injured at least 10 others.

item.title: Euronews: Salvage operation under way after cargo ship runs aground off French coast
item.description: French authorities are racing to prevent a stranded cargo ship from capsizing after it ran aground off the south-western coast. The Maltese-flagged vessel, which is carrying more than 100 tonnes of fuel, poses a potential pollution threat as salvage teams prepare to refloat it.

item.title: Euronews: Iran attacks US bases in Bahrain as its tankers get ready to break the US blockade
item.description: The “no war, no peace” US-Iran confrontation appears to be moving towards a possible breaking point as Iran increases its military actions in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, while its critical attempt to break the US military naval blockade in the Persian Gulf appears to be imminent.

item.title: Euronews: Video shows Mexican forces capturing 'El Chapo Isidro', FBI most-wanted cartel boss
item.description: Mexican special forces captured drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “Chapo Isidro”, during a raid in Sinaloa, with footage showing soldiers escorting him into an army vehicle.

item.title: Euronews: Thousands take to streets in Portugal, France and Spain over rising living costs
item.description: Thousands of people demonstrated in Portugal and France on Saturday, calling for higher wages, affordable housing and action to tackle the rising cost of living. In Lisbon, workers marched despite heavy rain, while trade unions, Yellow Vest activists and youth groups gathered in Paris.

item.title: Euronews: Paolo Bulgari, Italian jewellery tycoon, dies aged 89
item.description: The grandson of Bulgari's founder helped transform the family jewellery business into one of the world's most prestigious luxury brands. He led the Roman maison as chairman from 1984 and remained passionate about jewellery design throughout his life.

item.title: Euronews: New documentary: Princess Kate speaks candidly about how cancer changed her body and mind
item.description: The Princess of Wales opens up about the physical and emotional impact of her cancer diagnosis in a deeply personal BBC documentary. Kate also reflects on her recovery, finding hope amid uncertainty and learning to live with a new perspective on life.
